newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Generali premiums up 8.8pct in '96.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Generali premiums up 8.8pct in '96.

text.p: Premium income at the parent company of Italian insurance firm Generali rose by 8.8 percent in 1996 to over 11.4 trillion lire, the firm said in a statement following a board meeting.
Generali added that profits last year were "better" than in 1995. It did not give any profit figures. Generali's parent company made a net profit of 482.7 billion lire in 1995.

The company, the largest insurance firm in Italy, said at a group level its premiums rose 10.1 percent to 28.6 trillion lire. It said that its premium data took into account exchange rate fluctuations.

"Despite considerable losses (of over 300 billion lire) because of exchange rate conversions following the strengthening of the lira, which weighed on the economic accounts, the forecast of a better final result than (1995) can be confirmed," the Generali statement said.
At the parent level, life premium income rose 17.3 percent to 5.4 trillion lire, while non-life premiums rose 2.1 percent to more than six trillion lire.
The ratio between costs and premiums fell 0.8 percentage points last year, Generali said, without giving any figures.
Profits from undisclosed sales were some 520 billion lire. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
